item.title: Neanderthal men had a thing for modern human women, genomes show
item.description: When Neanderthal men encountered modern human women tens of thousands of years ago, they were apparently very interested. A new genomic analysis published in Science examined the X chromosomes of completed Neanderthal genomes and found them loaded with modern human DNA sequences — far more than you'd see on other chromosomes. — Read the rest The post Neanderthal men had a thing for modern human women, genomes show appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: Red Dwarf co-creator Rob Grant dead at 70
item.description: Rob Grant, co-creator of cult science-fiction comedy series Red Dwarf, died Wednesday at 70. His family announced his death at the fan site Ganymede & Titan. With much sadness, we have to announce that Rob Grant, co-creator of Red Dwarf, passed away suddenly yesterday afternoon (Wednesday 25th February 2026), a great loss to his family, friends and comedy fans across the world. — Read the rest The post Red Dwarf co-creator Rob Grant dead at 70 appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: The one thing that actually stops would-be dictators
item.description: What actually stops a would-be dictator? Political science research points to a single factor above all others: whether enough people can see the threat for what it is. That's the central argument from Zack Beauchamp, who researched democratic resilience at Penn's Perry World House. — Read the rest The post The one thing that actually stops would-be dictators appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: Stolen Gemini API key racks up $82,000 in 48 hours for solo dev
item.description: If someone steals your credit card and racks up fraudulent charges, your bank will reverse them. If someone steals your cloud API key and racks up $82,000 in compute charges over a weekend, you owe Google the money. That is the state of consumer protection in cloud computing in 2024. — Read the rest The post Stolen Gemini API key racks up $82,000 in 48 hours for solo dev appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: Magnesium helps migraines but the rest of the hype is shaky
item.description: Migraine sufferers may have the strongest reason to reach for that bottle of magnesium on their nightstand. A review of four randomized controlled trials, published in February 2025 in Neurological Sciences, found daily doses of 122 to 600mg cut migraine frequency by about 2.5 attacks per month and eased severity. — Read the rest The post Magnesium helps migraines but the rest of the hype is shaky appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: Neck surgery may help flush Alzheimer's toxins from brain
item.description: A report in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery proposes using a microsurgical technique called lymphovenous anastomosis (LVA) to help clear the toxic proteins that build up in Alzheimer's patients' brains. According to the study, it's a plumbing problem. item.title: Meet the Enshittificator, a man whose job is making your apps worse
item.description: Somewhere in Norway, a man goes to work every morning, sits down at his desk, and deliberately makes your favorite apps worse. His job title: Enshittificator. He comes from a proud family tradition — generations of people who make things shitty — but thanks to the internet, he can ruin things for millions of people simultaneously. — Read the rest The post Meet the Enshittificator, a man whose job is making your apps worse appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: Pope tells priests to stop using AI to write their sermons
item.description: Forget stochastic parrots: how about periphrastic priests? Pope Leo XIV, in an address in Rome, warned Catholic clergy against using AI to pad out their sermons: "To give a true homily is to share faith," Leo said. "[machines] will never be able to share faith." — Read the rest The post Pope tells priests to stop using AI to write their sermons appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: LAPD officer charged with disability fraud after skydiving adventures
item.description: Professional disability doesn't necessarily leave someone unable to move, walk or play: it only limits their ability to work. But an LAPD officer on disability benefits since he "hurt his elbow" on duty in 2023 should have thought through the consequences of continuing his skydiving trips. — Read the rest The post LAPD officer charged with disability fraud after skydiving adventures appeared first on Boing Boing.
